name: AccessibilityExplorer

states.name: Page Structure and Layout
states.description: The Accessibility Explorer has a vertical layout: header bar with title and status, connection bar (when disconnected), stats bar (when connected), a two-column main area (60% tree view, 40% details panel), and a bottom tabbed section for Query and AI Context. When disconnected, only the header, connection input, and an empty-state message are visible.
states.precondition: Connected to a target with a captured tree

states.name: Connection and Target Selection
states.description: Users connect to a desktop application by entering its window title (e.g., 'Notepad'), process ID (e.g., 'pid:1234'), or 'Desktop' for the entire desktop. The Connect button establishes the accessibility bridge via the Rust-native adapter. A status badge shows the connection state and backend name (UIA, ATSPI, or AX). After connecting, the tree is automatically captured. The connection bar disappears when connected and is replaced by Refresh and Disconnect buttons in the header.

states.name: Snapshot Statistics Bar
states.description: When connected with a captured tree, a stats bar shows the total node count, interactive node count, window title (if available), and generation number. This gives users a quick summary of the captured tree's scope.

states.name: Accessibility Tree Viewer
states.description: The left panel shows a hierarchical tree of accessibility nodes captured from the target application. Each node is rendered as a treeitem with: an expand/collapse chevron (for nodes with children), a color-coded role badge (blue for buttons/links, green for inputs, gray for text, transparent for containers, purple for others), the accessible name, and a monospace ref ID (e.g., '@e3'). Interactive elements have a small blue dot indicator and a subtle blue background tint. Clicking a node selects it (highlighted with primary ring) and shows its details in the right panel. Keyboard navigation supports Enter/Space to select, ArrowRight to expand, ArrowLeft to collapse.

states.name: Element Properties and Actions

requiredElements.textContains: Select a node to view details

states.description: The right panel shows the selected node's full properties organized in sections: Identity (Role, Name, Value, Description, Ref ID with copy button, Source), Bounds (x, y, width, height in a 4-column grid), State (badges for all 13 state flags — active flags in green/success, inactive in outline), Supported Patterns (purple badges), and Actions (Click, Focus, Type buttons). When no node is selected, the panel shows 'Select a node to view details'.

states.name: Query Panel
states.description: The bottom Query tab provides a search interface for filtering the accessibility tree. Users select a role from a dropdown (25 common roles including button, checkbox, combobox, textbox, etc.), enter a label substring, toggle 'Interactive only', and click Search. Results appear as a clickable list showing role badge, name, and ref ID. Clicking a result selects it in the tree and shows its details.

states.name: AI Context Panel
states.description: The 'AI Context' tab shows the exact text representation that AI workflow agents receive when using the native_accessibility step type's ai_context action. Users click 'Generate AI Context' to invoke a11y_ai_context with maxElements=50 and interactiveOnly=true. The output appears in a monospace code block. A Copy button copies the text to the clipboard. This lets users verify exactly what the AI sees.

states.name: Visual Design and Styling
states.description: The Accessibility Explorer uses the runner's standard design system: muted backgrounds for inputs (bg-muted/30), border-border for borders, primary color for active elements, foreground/muted-foreground for text hierarchy. Cards have border-border/30 header dividers. The overall page uses p-4 padding and gap-3 spacing between sections.

states.name: Keyboard Navigation
states.description: The tree view supports keyboard navigation: Tab to focus tree items, Enter or Space to select a node, ArrowRight to expand a collapsed node, ArrowLeft to collapse an expanded node. The target input supports Enter to submit. The type-text input supports Enter to send.

description: Accessibility Explorer — inspect and interact with native desktop accessibility trees from any running application. Users connect to a window by title, process ID, or 'Desktop', capture the accessibility tree via the Rust-native UIA (Windows), AT-SPI (Linux), or AX (macOS) adapter, browse elements in a hierarchical tree view with role-coded badges and expand/collapse, view full element properties and state flags, execute actions (Click, Focus, Type) via native accessibility patterns, query the tree by role/label/interactivity, and preview the AI Context output that workflow agents receive when using native_accessibility steps.
